raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything too fancy. On my 9 mu, I’ll still keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the safest in our place. Wheat and maize together keep grain coming, and if one season is not good, the other may still hold up. But I’ll leave a bit of land in cotton, same as before, because cotton can still bring cash if the price is not too bad. I don’t read those technical things much. I mostly look at what worked on my own fields and what the capable people in the village are doing. Fertilizer is expensive now, water from the well also costs money, so I won’t push too hard, but I also don’t dare cut too much. If wheat turns yellow or maize looks weak, then I add a bit more. My sons and younger people have some off-farm work, so I try to arrange things in the usual way and avoid jobs that need too much labor all at once.

For wheat, I’ll plant on time in October on 6 mu, using the usual local improved seed. I’ll put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once around jointing if the crop looks like it needs feeding. I’ll irrigate about 3 times if the weather is normal, because wheat here usually needs water and I have the well. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll sow summer maize quickly on the same 6 mu, no delay, because that window is very tight. I’ll do only light tillage or direct seeding after harvest to save time and labor. For cotton, I’ll keep 3 mu. Cotton takes more looking after, but on a small area I can still manage it with family labor. I won’t spend too much on cotton this year, because grain land comes first and cash is still tight.
